source: Sifrei Bamidbar 22:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 25:1; Onkelos Num 6:2
claim_en: THE THIRTY DAYS ARE THE DEFAULT; WOMEN, NOT MINORS; THE AGES OF VOWS; HANDLES AND EPITHETS. Against Num 30:3 (a vow binds by its term) the section teaches that a nazirite vow of one day or one moment binds THIRTY DAYS and three prohibitions — wine, the dead, the hair (row 22:1); the thirty derived three ways on the shelf — the default, the letters of 'he shall be' summed to thirty, the growth of the locks 'not less than thirty days' (row 25:1) — recorded as one number, three derivations; 'a man or a woman' equates women (the a-fortiori from the priests refuted), 'a man' excludes minors; 'if he declares' — one who knows to declare: a girl of eleven and a day examined, of twelve and a day her vows stand; a boy twelve and a day examined, thirteen and a day stand (Mishnah Niddah 5:6); willingly, by the identity with Lev 22:21; epithets and handles of nazirship are nazirship, and vows likened both ways (Mishnah Nazir 1:1); a father annuls his daughter's, a husband his wife's. Onkelos 'if he set apart to vow a vow of nazirship'; the declaring verb's four Torah seats and 'nazirite' at nine (computed).
middah: I2 (the identity 'declare'/'declare' with Lev 22:21 for a willing vow; the default and the ages read as data rows)

claim_en: WINE: THREE READINGS OF THE PAIR; MITZVAH WINE EQUATED; SELLING PERMITTED; THE TASTE AS THE SUBSTANCE. 'From wine and strong drink he shall separate' — the Sifrei: yayin IS shekhar, THE TORAH SPEAKS IN TWO TONGUES (as slaughter/sacrifice, fistful/lifting, sign/wonder); R. Elazar Hakappar: diluted and undiluted (from Num 28:7's altar-libation); ONKELOS: 'from wine NEW and OLD' — a third reading, none chosen, all recorded; mitzvah wine (the second tithe's) equated with optional wine — the mourner analogy and the officiating priest's a-fortiori both refuted, so the verse is needed; 'he shall not DRINK' — selling and healing permitted; vinegar equated with wine; 'any steeping of grapes' (the steeping-word's one pointing against 'minister' at seven — computed by the points): the TASTE regarded as the substance — a paradigm for every Torah prohibition by an a-fortiori from the nazirite's lighter bar (Pesachim 44b); 'moist' includes half-ripe; Issi b. Yehudah: each a liability in itself (Mishnah Nazir 6:1-2).
middah: I3 (the paradigm — the taste as the substance — built on the nazirite's lighter prohibition; the three readings of the pair recorded, none chosen)

claim_en: FROM KERNELS TO SKIN — GENERAL-PARTICULAR, COMBINATION, AND THE LIMIT ON A GENERAL THAT ADDS. 'Of all that is made from the vine of wine, from kernels to skin' (both words alone in the Tanakh, computed): an olive's bulk of all COMBINED — forty lashes; combination a paradigm for all prohibitions; leaves and sprouts excluded — 'fruit and residue of fruit' (R. Eliezer includes them); the minimum two kernels and one husk (R. Elazar b. Azariah); which is which — R. Yehudah / R. Yossi (the bell and its clapper — Nazir 34b); 'pained eating' does not exempt; and GENERAL-PARTICULAR on the whole clause with THE MIDDOT'S CASE LAW: a general that ADDS to the particular need not match the particular's nature unless Scripture specifies, as it does here (row 24:1). Onkelos 'from the pips to the PRESSED skins'.
middah: I4 (general-particular on 6:3-4, with the Sifrei's rule on the added general; the combination-paradigm I3 recorded beside)

claim_en: NO RAZOR; THE LOCKS ARE THE LEPER'S BY THE IDENTITY OF WORDING; THE A-FORTIORI THAT FAILS. 'A razor shall not pass over his head' (the clause's one seat, computed; Samson's and Samuel's razor another word): the shaver liable as the shaved; R. Yoshiyah — lashes also for tearing, plucking, trimming; R. Yonathan — the blade alone (Mishnah Nazir 6:3); the unqualified vow shaves on the thirty-first day, the thirtieth suffices; the eternal nazirite from 'all the days'; 'holy shall he be' = the hair (6:8 = the body); 'let grow the locks' — the leper's 'his head shall be loosed' (Lev 13:45) means GROWN LONG by the identity with the nazirite's locks (the root's six Torah seats, computed); and the days after the term before the offering equated with the term — for wine, for shaving (the a-fortiori refuted by the leper-nazirite's permitted shaving, refuted back by tumah): 'I HAVE NOT SUCCEEDED WITH MY A-FORTIORI' — the identity on the EXTRA 'nazirite' of 6:20 ('may a nazirite drink wine?') decides. Onkelos 'a shearing blade... growing the loose hair'.
middah: I2 (the identity 'locks'/'loosed' with Lev 13:45, and the identity on the superfluous 'nazirite' of 6:20 after the a-fortiori chain fails — the Sifrei's own words)

check.note: 'the locks' — the leper's word on the nazirite

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 26:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 27:1; Onkelos Num 6:6; Onkelos Num 6:7; Onkelos Num 6:8
claim_en: A DEAD SOUL IS A MAN; NOT FOR KIN, YES FOR THE UNBURIED; THE CROWN IS THE HIGH PRIEST'S WORD. 'Upon a dead soul he shall not come' (one seat; the high priest's 'upon all dead souls' at Lev 21:11 its pair — computed): a human, not a beast; R. Yishmael — 'he shall not COME', a tent-uncleanness (Onkelos 'he shall not ENTER' agrees); 'for his father and mother he shall not defile himself' — BUT FOR A CORPSE WITH NO ONE TO BURY IT HE DOES (the a-fortiori from the high priest refuted by the offering distinction, so the verse is needed); 'his brother', 'his sister' — the man going to his paschal lamb or his son's circumcision who hears of a death: not for kin, yes for the unburied (Berakhot 19b-20a); 'in their death' — not in their leprosy or discharge, and the high priest the same by the identity 'his mother'/'his mother'; 'the crown of his God on his head' — the crown-word at five Torah seats, four the high priest's plate and oil (Exod 29:6, 39:30, Lev 8:9, 21:12) and this (computed) — Onkelos gives him a diadem; with or without hair (R. Yonathan); 'holy is he' = the body (row 27:1).
middah: I2 (the identity 'his mother'/'his mother' between the nazirite and the high priest; the crown-word's seats computed)

check.note: 'the crown' — the high priest's word on the nazirite

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 28:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 28:2; Sifrei Bamidbar 29:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 29:2; Sifrei Bamidbar 30:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 31:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 31:2; Onkelos Num 6:9; Onkelos Num 6:10; Onkelos Num 6:11; Onkelos Num 6:12
claim_en: THE DEFILED NAZIRITE: CERTAIN NOT DOUBT; THE HEAD; THE SEVENTH IS THE SPRINKLING'S; THE EIGHTH BY THE IDENTITY; SHAVE THEN OFFER; THE SIN AGAINST THE SOUL DISPUTED; THE FIRST DAYS FALL. 'If one die on him' — a certain death, not a doubt (the sotah's doubt-as-certainty refused: the two laws cross — she equates doubt with certainty, not inadvertence with intent; he the reverse — a paired parameter on two engines, row 28:1); 'in a sudden instant' (one seat, computed) — inadvertent and unwitting; the wilful liable by 6:11; one who was clean and became unclean — not the cemetery-vower; 'shave his HEAD' — not all the hair; 'the day of his cleansing' = the sprinkling's day, the seventh; the eighth and after valid; SHAVE, THEN OFFER — reversed, not fulfilled (row 28:2); 'the eighth day' excludes the seventh, not the ninth — the a-fortiori refuted by the paschal window, the identity 'eighth day'/'eighth day' decides (row 29:1; Nazir 18a); turtledoves not substituted (Mishnah Kinnim 2:5); the priest designates, the owner too — an unqualified pair and a qualified (Mishnah Kinnim 1:1); 'he sinned against the soul' — he denied himself wine (and the faster by a-fortiori — Taanit 11a) / R. Yishmael: the dead soul (Onkelos 'upon the dead') — two arms recorded (row 30:1); 'the first days shall fall' (one seat, computed): defiled on the ninety-ninth day of a hundred — all void; on the hundredth or the first — not; TUMAH VOIDS ALL, SHAVING VOIDS THIRTY (Mishnah Nazir 3:3-4, 6:5); the leper's confirmation days not counted, the quarantine counted (Mishnah Nazir 7:3 — rows 31:1-2). Onkelos 'the first days shall be VOID'.
middah: I2 (the identity 'the eighth day'/'the eighth day' with Lev 22:27 after the a-fortiori fails; the crossed parameter with the sotah recorded; the rows' data read as they stand)

check.note: '[the first days] shall fall' — the voided count

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 31:3; Sifrei Bamidbar 25:1; Onkelos Num 6:20
claim_en: THE ARGUMENT GOES ROUND AND ROUND — THE EXTRA NAZIRITE DECIDES. The days after the term before the offering, equated with the term for TUMAH: from wine (refuted — tumah has a permitted act, the unburied corpse; wine none), from shaving (refuted — the shaver is equated for liability, the defiler not), refuted back by wine (the one who gives him to drink is not equated, yet equated) — 'AND THE ARGUMENT GOES ROUND': the a-fortiori chain cycles; 'and after, the nazirite may drink wine' (6:20, the clause's one seat, computed) — 'may a NAZIRITE drink wine?' the word is extra: the identity of wording 'nazirite' (6:12) / 'nazirite' (6:20) equates the days for tumah as for wine (row 31:3), the same identity that decided shaving (row 25:1). The middot's own case law twice on one chapter: a circular a-fortiori FAILS; a gezerah shavah — the identity of wording — on a superfluous word DECIDES (MIDDOT.md). Onkelos 'and after that the nazirite may drink wine'.
middah: I2 (the identity on the superfluous 'nazirite' of 6:20 — the Sifrei's own resolution after the a-fortiori cycles)

check.note: 'the nazirite' — the extra word the identity runs on

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 32:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 33:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 35:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 36:1; Onkelos Num 6:13; Onkelos Num 6:14; Onkelos Num 6:15; Onkelos Num 6:16; Onkelos Num 6:17; Onkelos Num 6:18; Onkelos Num 6:19
claim_en: HE BRINGS HIMSELF; THREE WHOLE ANIMALS; THE DOOR IS THE PEACE OFFERING'S — WHERE HE COOKS, THERE HE SHAVES; THE POT INSERTED. 'He shall bring HIM to the door' (the phrase's one seat, computed): do others bring him? He brings HIMSELF — one of R. Yishmael's three reflexive object-markers (Lev 22:16, Deut 34:6 — row 32:1); Onkelos 'he shall bring himself' keeps it; 'whole' thrice excludes the blemished — three animals, each a mitzvah (row 33:1); 'shave at the door of the tent of meeting' — Scripture means AFTER THE PEACE OFFERINGS (Lev 3:2's 'at the door'), not literally at the door (the a-fortiori from Exod 20:23's steps); R. Yitzchak — from 'on the fire under the sacrifice': IN THE PLACE WHERE HE COOKS IT, THERE HE SHAVES; the door must be open; under any of his offerings; outside too (row 35:1; Mishnah Nazir 6:8); Onkelos 6:18 inserts 'under THE POT of the holy slaughtering' — the translation and the Sifrei both put the shaving in the kitchen; 'the cooked shoulder' — whole / with the ram (row 36:1); on his palms after the shaving — the portion's second palms-verse (with 5:18, computed).
middah: plain (R. Yishmael's reflexive reading and the Sifrei's kitchen read as they stand; the inserted word cut from the shelf's bytes)

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 34:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 37:1; Onkelos Num 6:15; Onkelos Num 6:16; Onkelos Num 6:17; Onkelos Num 6:18; Onkelos Num 6:19; Onkelos Num 6:20
claim_en: THE ELEVENTH RULE STATED ON 6:20; LIBATIONS FOR THE VOWED. 'Holy to the priest beside the breast of waving and the thigh of lifting' (the pair's Torah seats Exod 29:27, Lev 7:34, 10:14-15, Num 6:20 — computed): the nazirite's peace offering was in Lev 7:34's general and departed for the SHOULDER — the breast and thigh would follow by an a-fortiori — so why written? 'WHATEVER WAS INCLUDED IN A GENERAL AND DEPARTED FROM IT FOR A NEW LEARNING MAY NOT BE RETURNED TO ITS GENERAL UNTIL SCRIPTURE EXPLICITLY RETURNS IT' — Rabbi Ishmael's eleventh rule in the Sifrei's own words on this verse (row 37:1); and on 6:15-17: 'a basket of unleavened bread' (general), 'cakes and wafers' (particular) — two kinds, not the thank offering's four; 'their libations' for the burnt and the peace, not the sin and the guilt — THE RAM DEPARTED FROM THE GENERAL TO TEACH ON THE GENERAL: offerings by vow and gift take libations (row 34:1 — the row whose head the export mistypes '6:150', placed by position). 'Lifting is compared to waving' — Onkelos' one verb for both (5:25, 6:20).
middah: I11 (the thing that departed to a new matter, not returned until Scripture returns it — stated by the Sifrei on 6:20; I8 and I4 on 6:15-17 recorded beside)

check.note: 'the waving' — the breast the eleventh rule keeps out

claim_en: THIS IS THE LAW — THE THIRD; THE OFFERING CONTINGENT ON THE NAZIRSHIP; WHAT HIS HAND ATTAINS; FIVE NAZIRSHIPS, FIVE SHAVINGS; THE LEPER-NAZIRITE'S ONE SHAVING REFUSED. The third 'this is the law' of the portion (computed; R. Yoshiyah / R. Yonathan again); 'his offering for his nazirship' — contingent on it, not the reverse; not others' offering; 'besides what his hand attains' (Onkelos 'what his hand reaches'): a hundred burnt and peace offerings as vowed, but not sin and guilt offerings — 'that he vows', the vowable kinds; 'five nazirships, one shaving' refused — one shaving each; and R. Eliezer b. Shamua and R. Yochanan HaSandlar to R. Shimon b. Yochai: a clean nazirite who is a leper — one shaving for both? NO, in every combination: the leper shaves to grow hair, the nazirite to remove it; before the blood, after; after the heifer's water, before — a four-way table of refusals (Nazir 60a-61a).
middah: plain (the Sifrei's rows read as they stand; the four-way refusal a verdict table for the exam)
